If it lives in AWS, this seat is responsible for it being correctly configured, properly monitored, and ready for an auditor to walk through. The platform runs on AWS and it handles PHI. That sentence carries the whole job. You configure the environments so that PHI moves only where it should move, encrypted at rest and in transit, audited at every hop, and tied back to a real identity that a HIPAA assessor can trace. You configure the networking so that a facility partner can route their on premises traffic into the company’s platform through a secure tunnel that holds up to scrutiny. This is also the seat that owns the daily operational reality of business continuity and workforce identity. Backups either ran clean or they did not. Restores either work or they have not been tested recently enough. Every employee and contractor has exactly the access they should have, or they do not. You own those answers, every day. Partnering closely with the engineering teams is an important part of this seat. You work alongside them on infrastructure decisions, and you own the operational reality of those decisions once they are made. You make sure the running system actually matches what the teams designed and agreed on. What You Will Own AWS account and organization configuration. You own AWS Organizations setup, account structure, service control policies, and the separation between production, staging, and development. You configure the landing zone, the guardrails, and the controls that keep one account's mistakes from leaking into another. Networking and connectivity. This is the heart of the seat. You own VPC design, subnet layout, route tables, security groups, NACLs, and the Transit Gateway topology that ties it all together. You build site to site VPN tunnels and Transit Gateway attachments that let facility partners and integration partners reach the company from their own networks without ever exposing PHI to the public internet. You can explain BGP routing on a whiteboard, and you have configured customer gateways for partners running every kind of edge device you can think of. Secure cross organization tunneling for PHI. Real facilities have their own IT infrastructure, and PHI has to move between their environment and this company under HIPAA rules. You design the tunnels. You configure the encryption. You document what flows where, and you can defend it to a compliance auditor. When a new facility partner needs to integrate, you are the one who walks their network team through the connection plan and gets it working. Compute and data infrastructure. You administer EC2 fleets, Aurora PostgreSQL clusters, RDS, DynamoDB, ElastiCache, and the MSK Kafka event spine that ties this company’s services together. You handle capacity planning, scaling configuration, patch management, and broker health. You know what to do when an Aurora instance starts behaving badly at 3 AM, or when a Kafka consumer lag chart starts climbing in the wrong direction. DNS and certificates.
